message.content:
The last common ancestor of a lion (*Panthera leo*) and a zebra (*Equus quagga*) is the most recent common ancestor of the two families **Felidae** (cats) and **Equidae** (horses).  
In other words, it is the last common ancestor of the two orders **Carnivora** (which contains cats, dogs, bears, etc.) and **Perissodactyla** (odd‑toed ungulates such as horses, rhinos, and tapirs).  

That ancestor would have lived roughly 50–60 million years ago during the early Eocene, when the mammalian lineages that would become carnivores and odd‑toed ungulates were already diverging. It was likely a small, generalized mammal that eventually split into the distinct lineages that led to modern lions and zebras.
